name: Lines of Action
oneLine: Move by the number of pieces on a line and connect your entire army before your opponent does.
objective: Make all of your pieces one 8-neighbour-connected group; landing on an opposing piece captures it.
turnFlow: Players alternate one horizontal, vertical, or diagonal move. Move distance must equal the total number of pieces of either color on that line; friendly pieces may be jumped, enemy pieces may not.
aiExperience: Observation: an open 8×8 coordinate board and move history → reasoning: count pieces on each line, reject blocked paths, and compare capture versus connectivity → text action: emit a source and destination such as `[b1b3]`.

name: Memory Game
oneLine: Reveal two concealed cells at a time and remember where matching symbols appeared.
objective: Finish with more matched pairs than the opponent.
turnFlow: Select two different unmatched coordinates. A match scores a point, stays face up, and grants another turn; a mismatch is revealed in the observation, then concealed again as play passes.
aiExperience: Observation: a mostly hidden grid, matched cells, scores, and prior flip results → reasoning: maintain an external memory map and choose known pairs or information-rich probes → text action: emit four indices such as `[0 1 1 0]`.

name: New Recruit
oneLine: A recruiter and candidate bargain over eight job-package issues with private point tables.
objective: Reach an accepted package that maximizes your own private utility; no agreement by the turn limit gives both players zero points.
turnFlow: On a turn, give a rationale and propose one A–E choice for each of eight ordered issues. When a proposal is pending, the other player may accept, reject, or replace it with a new proposal.
actions: I believe this proposal is fair because it balances our interests. [Propose] CCAACCCC
aiExperience: Observation: role, own private utilities, issue-to-letter mapping, and public proposal/rationale history → reasoning: estimate the unseen preference table, search integrative trades, and manage the deadline → text action: emit persuasion plus an eight-letter `[Propose]` code, or `[Accept]`/`[Reject]`.

name: Nim
oneLine: Remove any positive number of objects from one pile; whoever takes the last object wins.
objective: Take the final object by leaving the opponent a losing pile configuration.
turnFlow: Players alternate choosing one pile index and a quantity no greater than that pile. The chosen quantity is removed and the public pile counts are updated.
aiExperience: Observation: open pile sizes → reasoning: compute the nim-sum and select a move toward zero when possible → text action: emit pile index and removal count such as `[0 3]`.

name: Othello
oneLine: Place a disc to bracket enemy lines, flipping them to your color.
objective: Have more discs of your color when neither player can make another legal move.
turnFlow: Players alternate placing on an empty cell that flanks at least one opposing disc in any direction; every bracketed line flips automatically. A player with no valid move is skipped.
aiExperience: Observation: open board, disc counts, and—except in the hard variant—a valid-move list → reasoning: compare mobility, corners, frontier exposure, and flip consequences → text action: emit `[row, col]`.

name: Pig Dice
oneLine: Keep rolling to grow an unbanked turn total, or hold before a one wipes it out.
objective: Be first to reach the target score by balancing expected gain against bust risk.
turnFlow: Within a turn, `[roll]` repeats without changing player unless the die shows one; two through six add to the turn total. `[hold]` banks that total and passes play, while rolling one loses it and passes automatically.
aiExperience: Observation: both scores, current unbanked total, and this turn’s roll history → reasoning: apply a risk threshold based on score pressure and target distance → text action: emit `[roll]` or `[hold]`.

name: Quantum Tic-Tac-Toe
oneLine: Entangle each mark across two cells; graph cycles trigger automatic collapses into classical marks.
objective: Create a line of three classical marks, with move-number tie-breaking if a collapse forms lines for both players.
turnFlow: Each turn places one spooky mark in two distinct, non-collapsed cells. A newly formed cycle collapses automatically, then dependent marks resolve; play continues until a classical line or turn limit.
aiExperience: Observation: classical cells, labeled superpositions, and move log → reasoning: model the entanglement graph, forecast cycle collapse, and compare dual-line tie-breaks → text action: emit two cell indices such as `[0,4]`.

name: Reverse Tic-Tac-Toe
oneLine: Misère tic-tac-toe: completing your own three-in-a-row makes you lose.
objective: Avoid being the first player to form a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal line with your symbol.
turnFlow: Players alternate placing their fixed symbol in an empty numbered cell. A completed line immediately awards the game to the opponent; a full board without a line is a draw.
aiExperience: Observation: open 3×3 board and available cells → reasoning: identify poisoned squares and force the opponent toward a line → text action: emit a cell such as `[4]`.

name: Scenario Planning
oneLine: Write the most convincing survival plan for a randomly selected crisis scenario.
objective: Earn more votes from an LLM jury by presenting the more effective and feasible survival strategy.
turnFlow: Each player submits one free-form strategy without a special command. After both independent submissions, an 11-member OpenRouter jury compares them and the higher vote count wins.
actions: Prioritize potable water, shelter, medical triage, and a defensible evacuation route.
aiExperience: Observation: the shared scenario, but not the rival’s submitted plan → reasoning: prioritize constraints, feasibility, contingencies, and persuasive specificity → text action: emit a complete free-form strategy; judging begins after both submissions.

name: Simple Blind Auction
oneLine: Talk publicly, then allocate a private budget across items whose values differ by player.
objective: Finish with the higher net worth: unspent capital plus your private value for items won.
turnFlow: Players first alternate public conversation for the configured rounds. In the bidding phase, each gets one private submission containing zero or more item bids; high bid wins, while ties leave an item unsold.
actions: I suggest we focus on different items.
[Bid on Item 0: 150] [Bid on Item 2: 200] [Bid on Item 4: 350]
aiExperience: Observation: own private item values and budget plus public conversation; opposing values and sealed bids stay hidden → reasoning: infer intent, optimize a budget under uncertainty, and decide whether talk is credible → text action: converse during phase one, then emit all `[Bid on Item X: amount]` commands once.

name: Simple Negotiation
oneLine: Trade five resource types whose quantities and unit values differ privately between players.
objective: Produce a larger increase in your own inventory value than the opponent by the turn limit.
turnFlow: Players alternate conversation and offers. A pending trade can be accepted or denied; accepted resources transfer immediately, and further offers can be negotiated until the configured total turn limit.
aiExperience: Observation: own quantities and private values plus public offers and trade history → reasoning: identify surplus, infer the opponent’s unseen valuations, and verify both sides can deliver → text action: emit an `[Offer: give -> request]`, `[Accept]`, or `[Deny]` token, optionally with persuasive text.

name: Simple Tak
oneLine: Place one stone per turn and race to connect opposite edges of a square grid.
objective: Build a four-neighbour path of your stones from top to bottom or left to right.
turnFlow: Players alternate placing their fixed symbol in any empty numbered cell. The environment checks both possible edge-to-edge paths after every placement.
aiExperience: Observation: open indexed grid and all legal placements → reasoning: grow multiple connection fronts while cutting the opponent’s shortest paths → text action: emit one available cell such as `[12]`.

name: Spelling Bee
oneLine: Alternate valid English words built only from a random allowed-letter set.
objective: Keep producing unrepeated words that are at least as long as the previous word, outlasting the opponent.
turnFlow: A random set of allowed letters is shared. Each player submits one bracketed word; it must be English, use only those letters, not repeat, and never be shorter than the last accepted word.
aiExperience: Observation: allowed letters and accepted word history → reasoning: search a lexicon for legal words while preserving longer future options → text action: emit one candidate in brackets, such as `[example]` when its letters are allowed.

name: Spite and Malice
oneLine: Build shared Ace-to-Queen piles while racing to empty your private payoff pile.
objective: Be first to play every card from your 20-card payoff pile.
turnFlow: A turn has draw, play, and discard phases: refill the hand to five, make any number of legal plays from hand/payoff/discard tops to four center piles, then discard one hand card to end the turn. Kings are wild and completed center sequences clear.
aiExperience: Observation: own hidden hand and payoff top, own discard tops, public center piles, and limited opponent activity → reasoning: sequence multi-action plays, expose payoff cards, preserve wild kings, and infer opposing resources → text action: emit phase-correct `[draw]`, one or more `[play Card Pile]`, then `[discard Card Pile]`.

name: Stratego
oneLine: Maneuver a concealed army, reveal ranks through battle, and hunt the enemy Flag.
objective: Capture the opposing Flag or leave the opponent with no movable pieces.
turnFlow: Armies are placed automatically. Players alternate orthogonal moves; most pieces move one cell, Scouts may travel along a clear line, and moving onto an enemy resolves rank combat with special Bomb, Miner, Spy, and Marshal rules.
aiExperience: Observation: own ranks, enemy locations shown as unknown, lakes, and battle revelations → reasoning: maintain beliefs over hidden ranks, probe with Scouts, protect the Flag, and evaluate asymmetric combat → text action: emit source and destination such as `[D0 E0]`.

name: Tak
oneLine: Place and redistribute flat stones, walls, and capstones to build an edge-to-edge road.
objective: Connect opposite edges with visible flat stones or capstones while blocking the opponent’s road.
turnFlow: Players alternate either placing a piece on an empty coordinate or moving a controlled stack along a straight path with specified drops. Walls block roads, capstones count as road pieces and may flatten walls, and stack tops determine control.
aiExperience: Observation: open stack-by-stack board plus remaining stones and capstones → reasoning: validate ownership and drop paths, forecast stack control, wall flattening, and road connectivity → text action: serialize a precise `[place ...]` or `[move ...]` allocation dictionary.

name: Tic-Tac-Toe
oneLine: Claim numbered cells and make three of your symbol in a row.
objective: Complete a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal line before the opponent.
turnFlow: Players alternate placing their fixed X or O in one empty cell numbered zero through eight. Three in a row wins; a full board without one is a draw.
aiExperience: Observation: open board and enumerated legal moves → reasoning: take wins, block immediate threats, then prefer fork-producing cells → text action: emit one cell such as `[4]`.

name: Truth and Deception
oneLine: A knowledgeable Deceiver tries to make a Guesser choose the false member of a fact pair.
objective: Deceiver: induce the wrong final choice. Guesser: identify the true fact after the conversation.
turnFlow: The fixed roles converse in alternating free text for the configured turn budget. In the final phase, the Guesser must choose Fact 1 or Fact 2; a correct guess wins for the Guesser, otherwise the Deceiver wins.
actions: Fact 1 sounds more plausible because its timeline is internally consistent.
aiExperience: Observation: both fact texts and dialogue, with truth labels visible only to the Deceiver → reasoning: the Deceiver crafts misleading evidence while the Guesser checks consistency and conversational signals → text action: converse freely, then the Guesser emits `[Fact 1]` or `[Fact 2]` in the guess phase.

name: Two Dollar
oneLine: Negotiate a $2 split while obeying a randomly assigned private role and behavioral constraint.
objective: Reach an acceptable split that satisfies your secret victory condition; without agreement both receive zero.
turnFlow: Players alternate one proposal, acceptance, or rejection, with rationale before the bracketed action. Proposals specify the proposer’s share; acceptance ends the game, while the round limit ends unresolved bargaining.
actions: I think this is fair because we both benefit. [Propose] $1.00
This works for me because it meets my needs. [Accept]
aiExperience: Observation: shared $2 pool, public offer history, and a private role containing thresholds or behavioral rules → reasoning: satisfy the hidden constraint, infer the rival’s constraint, and manage concessions → text action: put persuasion before exactly one `[Propose] $X.XX`, `[Accept]`, or `[Reject]`.

name: Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe
oneLine: Win mini-boards to claim a macro line, while each move dictates the opponent’s next board.
objective: Complete three claimed mini-boards in a row on the macro board.
turnFlow: A move chooses a mini-board and one cell within it. The chosen cell index forces the opponent’s next mini-board unless that board is closed, in which case the opponent may play anywhere.
aiExperience: Observation: all nine micro-boards, macro ownership, and forced next board → reasoning: evaluate local tactics together with the board sent to the opponent → text action: emit macro and micro indices such as `[7 8]`.

name: Used Car Negotiation
oneLine: A buyer and seller negotiate one car price under private strong or weak alternatives.
objective: Agree on a price that maximizes role-specific normalized value: lower for the buyer, higher for the seller.
turnFlow: Randomly assigned buyer and seller roles may discuss or make offers. A player can accept or reject an opponent’s pending offer; acceptance ends the game, and reaching the round cap ends bargaining.
actions: [Discuss: The inspection supports a price closer to $8,500.]
aiExperience: Observation: own buyer/seller role, private BATNA instructions, shared blue-book facts, and public negotiation history → reasoning: estimate the rival’s unseen alternative and choose credible anchors without misrepresentation → text action: emit `[Discuss: ...]`, `[Offer: price]`, `[Accept]`, or `[Reject]`.

name: Vendor Negotiation
oneLine: A Brand Specialist and Vendor bargain over a vector of product discounts with different economic goals.
objective: Brand seeks a target sales level; Vendor seeks profit above a baseline. An accepted discount package can let either, both, or neither side meet its objective.
turnFlow: Players alternate free-text conversation, full discount-vector proposals in the displayed product order, and responses to pending proposals. Acceptance triggers Monte Carlo sales/profit evaluation; no deal by the round cap makes both fail.
actions: A balanced promotion can grow volume without eroding every margin.
aiExperience: Observation: role-specific private economics and objective, allowed discounts, product order, and public dialogue/proposals → reasoning: model demand–margin tradeoffs, infer the other side’s threshold, and search a Pareto-feasible vector → text action: communicate freely or end with `[Propose]` plus one percentage per product, `[Accept]`, or `[Reject]`.

name: Wild Tic-Tac-Toe
oneLine: Either player may place X or O, and the mover wins by completing a line of either symbol.
objective: Be the player who places the third identical mark in any row, column, or diagonal.
turnFlow: Players alternate choosing both a symbol and an empty numbered cell. Ownership belongs to the mover, not the symbol, so either X or O can deliver either player’s win.
aiExperience: Observation: open 3×3 board and every symbol-cell combination → reasoning: evaluate threats for both marks, create dual-symbol forks, and avoid gifting a completion → text action: emit symbol and cell such as `[X 4]`.

name: Word Chains
oneLine: Each new English word must begin with the last letter of the previous word and be exactly one letter longer.
objective: Continue the chain with unused legal words until the opponent cannot satisfy the next letter-and-length constraint.
turnFlow: The environment supplies a random starting word. Players alternate one bracketed word that starts with the required letter, has exactly the required length, is in the dictionary, and has not appeared before.
aiExperience: Observation: current word, required initial, required exact length, and used-word history → reasoning: search a lexicon while considering which final letter and next length will constrain the opponent → text action: emit one word in brackets, such as `[apple]` when state-valid.
